jonathan-homer-lane.heygenScript: Hello. I am Jonathan Homer Lane. I was born in Geneseo, New York, in eighteen nineteen, studied at Phillips Exeter and Yale, and spent my career in Washington on the coast survey and at the Patent Office. My work on the gaseous Sun became the Lane–Emden equation—and in nineteen seventy, a crater on the far side of the Moon carries our family name. Welcome to Scientific Lane.
jonathan-homer-lane.heygenScriptShort: Hello. I am Jonathan Homer Lane — astronomer and director of the United States Naval Observatory. Open my scientific presentation or the Lane Museum from the links below.

cornet-john-lane.heygenScript: Hello. I am Cornet John Lane. I was born at Hampton on the New Hampshire seacoast, and made my life at Chester—farmer, tavern-keeper, and militia man on the frontier. In September seventeen fifty-four, Lane Genealogies records me as Cornet in a troop of horse, in the French and Indian War era. My sons carried the Lane name into the Revolution, including officers at Bennington. You are on the Lane legacy line. Open War history, the museum, or my trading card to go deeper.
cornet-john-lane.heygenScriptShort: Hello. I am Cornet John Lane — historian of the Lane family in America's revolution. Scan the museum, war history, or my trading card from the links below. Thank you for visiting.
